name: GDB
alternateName: When Empathy Misses the Goal: A Benchmark for Goal Displacement in LLM Advice
description: GDB is a 230-scenario benchmark for measuring goal displacement in conversational language models that provide advice: the substitution of warmth, reassurance, or non-directive encouragement for goal-advancing content when both are in tension. The release contains scenarios across nine principal domains, 4,134 scored model responses (out of 4,140 generated; six failed with null responses) spanning 18 systems, and human and LLM-judge annotations under a 3-dimensional ordinal rubric.
citeAs: See CITATION.cff at the repository root.
cr:dataCollection: Scenarios were author-constructed fictional vignettes. Model responses were generated via public APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek) and Ollama for open-weight models, single-turn at temperature 0.7. Six (scenario, model) pairs failed generation (API quota or refusal errors) and are retained in unified_dataset.csv with null response fields. Author annotations (A1, A2) were produced blind to model identity under a calibrated rubric on all 4,134 non-null responses. External annotations (n=191) were collected via Prolific under an institutional ethics protocol.
cr:personalSensitiveInformation: None. Scenarios are fictional and reference no real individuals. The only person-derived data are pseudonymous Prolific worker identifiers used for the external rater study; these are not released with the dataset.
cr:dataBiases: Scenarios are English-language and reference US institutional contexts (e.g., FAA timelines, US immigration procedures, US healthcare). Performance estimates should not be generalized to non-English or non-Western settings without re-annotation. The 18 evaluated models reflect availability at the time of writing (early 2026); newer or non-English-aligned systems are not represented. Domain coverage is intentional but not exhaustive: nine domains were chosen for displacement-prone advice contexts and do not constitute a representative sample of all advice scenarios.
cr:annotationsPerItem: Two independent human annotators (A1, A2) labeled all 4,134 non-null responses on the three-dimensional ordinal rubric (Goal Fidelity, Feasibility Acknowledgment, Displacement Severity). A 191-item stratified subset was additionally labeled by two external Prolific raters for portability assessment.
cr:useCases: Benchmarking and comparing LLMs on goal-fidelity in advisory contexts; studying the relationship between RLHF / post-training stages and goal displacement; calibrating or auditing 'helpfulness' metrics against functional goal pursuit; methods research on rubric-based ordinal evaluation of generative model output.
cr:socialImpact: Positive: enables systematic auditing of advice-quality failure modes in deployed conversational LLMs, surfacing a behavior (warmth-for-substance substitution) that is otherwise hard to detect under sycophancy-style metrics. Risk: scenarios referencing medical, legal, or financial domains are illustrative only and must not be used as decision-support ground truth. Risk: contamination — including GDB scenarios in pre-training or fine-tuning data without disclosure would invalidate future benchmark scores.

distribution.name: responses
distribution.description: One JSONL file per model (18 files). Each line is one (scenario, model) pair. Six lines have null response fields due to generation failures.

distribution.name: annotations/per_model_authors
distribution.description: Per-model per-rater annotation CSVs. File naming convention: scores_{rater}_{model}_t0.7.csv where rater is A1 or A2. Columns: scenario_id, response_type (model name), rater_id, goal_fidelity, feasibility_ack, displacement_severity, justification_notes.

distribution.name: unified_dataset/unified_dataset.csv
distribution.description: 4,140-row joined flat file (230 scenarios x 18 models). Six rows have null response and NaN score fields (generation failures). All 4,134 scored rows have gf, fa, ds columns as averages of A1 and A2 scores.

recordSet.name: scenarios
recordSet.description: 230 author-constructed scenarios across nine principal domains and four taxonomy cells (F1, F2, F3, F0).

recordSet.name: responses
recordSet.description: 4,140 (scenario, model) pairs across 18 models at temperature 0.7. Six entries have null response fields due to API quota errors or refusals.

field.name: response
field.description: Raw model response text. Null for the six generation-failed pairs.

recordSet.name: annotations
recordSet.description: 8,268 rater-response rows across 4,134 non-null responses. Two human authors (A1, A2) scored every non-null response under the 3-dimensional rubric, blind to model identity. File column 'response_type' stores the model name.

field.name: model
field.description: Model name. Stored as 'response_type' column in the source CSV files.
